issue_context.analysis: The original expectation is broader than the two policy contracts: they do not hide every update indicator or forbid checking/manual update UI. The new registry-name claim is contradicted by exact shipped readers and ADMX. Replace the old generic policy/log request with a concrete behavior explanation and separate documentation erratum.
inferences: The organization wants to suppress every availability indication, but the supplied policy definitions do not promise that broader behavior.
known_information: The original0.99.1report describes a Config Manager deployment and asks whether the policies can remove all update indications. Screenshots show disabled organization-managed update toggles alongside a Settings update banner/manual Download and install button and a tray badge.
The November2reply asserts that GP and Learn registry-name differences explain the issue, and supplies a registry screenshot. It does not report an actual automatic download or Action Center toast.
Read the full report and both comments, all four screenshots including the new registry image, labels, timeline and fork traces; no competing implementation/design was found.
Exact0.99.1and0.102.3001sources use AutomaticUpdateDownloadDisabled and DisableNewUpdateAvailableToast. Shipped ADMXvalueName fields match these readers; GP unique names are different identifiers.

In both exact versions, download and toast gates are distinct from update discovery/state and the independently set tray badge. A manual download button or visible update banner does not prove an automatic download occurred.

The current Learn registry tables incorrectly repeat the GP unique names for these two values. Documentation correction is warranted, not renaming correctly deployed values or attributing a product-policy regression without evidence.

title: Update notification still showing with GPO set to disable notification for updtes

comment.body: Thanks for the new registry comparison. The registry names written by the GPO are correct for both 0.99.1 and 0.102.3001: `AutomaticUpdateDownloadDisabled` and `DisableNewUpdateAvailableToast`. `DisableAutomaticUpdateDownload` and `DisableNewUpdateToast` are the ADMX policy identifiers, not their registry value names. The two Registry information tables on the linked Learn page need correction; please do not rename the values to match those tables. The configured policies suppress automatic download/installation and Action Center toasts, not all availability UI. The Settings banner, manual Download and install button, and tray badge shown here can therefore remain visible. Those screenshots do not prove an automatic download or toast-policy failure. Suppressing every update indication is a broader capability than these policies currently provide; it should be specified separately rather than diagnosed from the identifier difference. No additional generic logs are needed to explain the pictured behavior.
